header: aka is building identity for a world where AI agents work alongside people. I designed and built prototypes in Vue to explore what it could look like for humans and agents to share an identity, from watching an agent work to giving it access to real accounts.

media.name: patch_demo.mp4
media.title: An agent’s activity log, paired with an illustration that moves while it works

layout.title: Seeing an agent at work
text: Agents work in the background, which makes them easy to forget. The first question was simple. What if you could see an agent at work?

I paired two views. A plain activity log lists each step as it happens, with a timestamp. Beside it, an abstract illustration moves while the agent works. The log is for people who want the detail. The illustration tells everyone else, at a glance, that something is happening. It isn’t a literal picture of the work, more a signal that something is underway.
The open question: does seeing the process build trust, or just add noise?

layout.title: Sharing an agent
text: If you tell a coworker about your workflow, they should be able to try it themselves. From an agent’s public profile, one click on “Use this Agent” shows what it does and which apps it needs, like HubSpot and Slack. Then you can add it as is or customize it first.

media.name: add_patch.png
media.title: Try someone else’s agent as is, or customize it first

layout.title: Building an agent with words
text: Most people can’t describe an agent as a workflow, but they can say what they want done. So in this exploration, you spin one up just by describing the job. Key words are highlighted as they’re recognized: Slack and Google Docs become integrations, and scan and summarize become actions. Before anything runs, the exact access the agent will need, like reading Slack messages or writing to Google Docs, is spelled out underneath.

Later, its steps are laid out in order, so it’s easy to see what your agent is doing or change it: a weekly schedule, scanning 23 Slack channels, pulling out complaints, ranking them, and writing the report. Or change it with words.

layout.title: AI-enabled services
text: After a few months of exploring, we decided to focus first on AI-enabled services: companies that do work on behalf of their clients every day.
For Rivet, aka’s first client, I explored onboarding flows and interfaces that let tax accountants act on behalf of their clients, using the clients’ own credentials.

layout.title: Result
text: Ultimately, aka decided to take the product in a different direction, so these explorations stayed explorations.
